No repository files were changed; no format, verification script, build, commit, push, GitHub comment or merge was performed.

S2. MATERIAL FINDING 1: stale validation is not bound to the head used by later writes; concurrent progress can be overwritten and a stale copy can be restamped as current. Governing invariant: ADR 0012 single writer/no silent timeline rewrite, parent acceptance that a behind-head restored/forked copy cannot sync/release over head, ADR 0020 state integrity and section 5.9 capability truthfulness. Locations: packages/core/src/character/characterCustody.ts:364-366, :447-485, :761-805; appendRevision at packages/core/src/character/characterRegistry.ts:351-380 does not compare against a validated expected head. The already-held acquire branch re-reads the NEW head at :773 and stamps it at :780 without proving this sheet matches that head.

Concrete reproducer: /tmp/pr711-final-review/probe.test.ts and race-worker.mts, with real separate SQLite connections and a second Node/tsx process. The worker pauses after an actual headRevision query returns revision 1, returning that unmodified query result after the barrier (simulates process preemption, not invented data). Original and snapshot copy both have stamp 1; original progresses to level 3, copy to level 2. While copy is paused in its guard, original sync commits revision 2/level 3. Resume the worker: direct copy sync appends revision 3/level 2 and stamps 3; original now classifies stale-copy. In the acquire variant the worker instead returns already-held and stamps 2 onto its level-2 sheet while head is level 3; ordinary subsequent release commits revision 3/level 2. Outputs: /tmp/pr711-final-review/sync-race-evidence.json and acquire-race-evidence.json. This contradicts inventory :2445 and PR prose saying first sync wins and the other becomes stale; the later writer actually wins and can launder its stamp.

Sibling/state-dimension check: reproduced idle acquisition too. Pause an idle camp-a copy after loading revision-1 sheet; camp-b checks out, advances to level 3, and releases revision 2; camp-a then returns acquired and stamps 2 onto its level-1 sheet. Its release appends revision 3/level 1 (idle-race-evidence.json). Sync-back and release share the vulnerable guard; acquire has both idle and already-held variants. Owner: custody/registry orchestration in this PR. Required next state: make validation and registry append linearizable against custody/head, and bind an acquire stamp to the revision actually validated rather than an unvalidated re-read; concurrent changes must refuse/retry instead of granting freshness. Permanent evidence should be a generalized interleaving invariant over idle/already-held and acquire/sync/release, preserving both stale refusal and valid original progress, rather than retaining these exact level fixtures or /tmp barrier machinery. Material repair requires fresh full review.
S3. MATERIAL FINDING 2: the idle conflict path selects the checkout revision instead of the restored synchronized revision, so the advertised keep-this-campaign-version fork can discard already-synchronized progress. Governing authority: ADR 0012:190-196 requires branching the campaign's current (or explicitly chosen) revision to keep playing that campaign's version; parent design includes already-held AND idle paths, and this review explicitly includes fork/CLI resume. Location: packages/core/src/character/characterCustody.ts:692 still returns metadata.sourceRevision, unlike the repaired held branch :665-670 that uses readSyncedRevision. Consumers: packages/cli/src/playCharacter.ts:480-487, :495 and :531; packages/cli/src/playFork.ts:70-83. No player-selected historical revision overrides it in this resume flow.

Concrete repro in /tmp/pr711-final-review/probe.test.ts, output idle-fork-evidence.json: checkout revision 1/level 1; play to level 2 and release, producing registry revision 2 and campaign stamp 2 (metadata.sourceRevision stays 1); snapshot this fully synchronized campaign; advance original to revision 3/level 3 and release, leaving custody idle; materialize the snapshot and choose fork through activateCampaignCustody. Restored sheet is exactly level 2 at stamp 2, but idle classification reports localRevision 1, prompt says this campaign is revision 1 and offers keep this campaign's version, and fork attaches level 1 with parent mira@1. Original head stays level 3; the fork silently loses the restored level-2 state. In contrast, the already-held sibling reports stamp 2 and forks level 2, as independently probed. This is a pre-existing idle selection defect left exposed by the asymmetric repair, not a claim that the idle line was introduced in this commit. It belongs to the explicitly requested whole-path review and violates the same resolution contract. Owner: custody classification and its CLI consumer. Closure: use the durable synchronized revision consistently for the fully synchronized restored copy in both custody states, preserving the documented legacy fallback, and keep the fork's presented/selected revision truthful. Permanent evidence should be a generalized invariant with syncedRevision > sourceRevision across idle and held classifications and the real fork consumer, rather than this exact level example. No unsynchronized-sheet interpretation is needed for this reproducer. Material repair requires fresh full review.

S4. NON-MATERIAL observations / passing boundaries (no additional finding): the sequential A2-F3 example is repaired for stamped copies. The campaign-side table is live retained product implementation, not temporary proof scaffolding. serializeCampaign enumerates actual sqlite_master tables (persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts:53-61), and a real CheckpointStore/Dolt round trip and fork preserved campaign_id, sheet and synced revision 2 while registry head was 3. CLI EOF/cancel left it untouched; explicit catch-up adopted head and stamped it; held-path explicit fork created a new independent identity without changing original head. Original stamp-at-head unsynchronized progress resumed and released successfully. An injected failure on the campaign stamp AFTER the real registry append, followed by database close/reopen, recovered through sheet-equals-head restamping and then accepted further progress. Ordered sequential checkout/catch-up/acquire/sync/release writes have the intended recovery cases; S2 identifies the demonstrated concurrent-ordering exception. Legacy unstamped behavior matches the explicitly authorized residual.
